summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with Child's class B alcoholic cirrhosis, portal hypertension, ascites, and hepatic encephalopathy was admitted for dizziness, diarrhea, and acute worsening of chronic abdominal and back pain. She had been recently discharged after treatment for hepatic encephalopathy and a suspected UTI. On admission, she reported watery diarrhea with black residue at the end, though stool tested negative for C. difficile. Her mental status was variable but consistent with baseline encephalopathy. Labs showed elevated WBC that improved by discharge. Imaging revealed cirrhosis with trace ascites and no acute pathology. Diuretics were held initially due to diarrhea but restarted before discharge. Symptoms resolved during the hospital stay, and she was discharged home with follow-up planned. Pending stool and blood cultures remained unresolved at discharge.
